title: Register C5.0 and Cubist engine arguments; pass C5.0Control() args to the control object
description:
**Registrations.** Engine arguments are now registered with `parsnip::set_model_arg()`, replacing the custom `tunable.C5_rules()` and `tunable.cubist_rules()` methods (and `c5_rules_engine_args` / `add_engine_parameters()`).

- `C5_rules()` / C5.0: `CF` (`confidence_factor()`), `noGlobalPruning` (`no_global_pruning()`), `winnow` (`predictor_winnowing()`), `fuzzyThreshold` (`fuzzy_thresholding()`), `bands` (`rule_bands()`).
- `cubist_rules()` / Cubist: `extrapolation` (`extrapolation()`), `unbiased` (`unbiased_rules()`).
- Non-default main-argument ranges from the old methods moved into the registrations:
  - C5.0 `trees`: `c(1, 100)`.
  - C5.0 `min_n`: `c(2, 40)`.
  - Cubist `committees`: `c(1, 100)`.
  - Cubist `neighbors`: `c(0, 9)`.

The engine arguments now always appear in `tunable()` with `component_id = "engine"`, as with other parsnip engines. Previously they appeared only if one was already marked `tune()`.

**Bug fix in `c5_fit()`.** Engine arguments such as `CF` or `winnow` were passed to `C50::C5.0()` directly, which ignores them, so tuning them had no effect. They are now put into `C50::C5.0Control()`.

- An explicit `control` argument is now actually modified (`minCases`, default seed, `earlyStopping = FALSE`). Previously the modification was applied to the quosure and lost.
- Defaults are no longer dropped when other engine args are supplied.
- Passing both `control` and control arguments now errors.

**Test fix.** The Cubist "argument/call assembly" tests now derive their expected control lists from `Cubist::cubistControl()`. They had hard-coded the fields, and failed on `main` once Cubist added `strip_time_stamps`.

title: Pass objective as passible engine argument for rule_fit()
description:
Related to #95 

There are still issues that make it continue to be difficult to make the xrf and rules fits the same. 

One other issue is that tidymodels uses a one-hot encoding when creating dummy variables for xgboost while xrf uses the standard full-rank encoding produced by `model.matrix()`. 

This PR solves the objective issue and updates some tests for the new xgboost API. The probability-based tests now use a tolerance since their results are very similar. I've removed or commented out tests based on hard class predictions, as we have no way of ensuring that those will be equal (but plan to resolve this discrepancy).

title: Add "Supported By Posit" badge to rules website
description:
## Overview

This PR adds the "Supported by Posit" badge to the rules website.

## Background

We've recently started adding a "Supported by Posit" badge across all Posit package websites to create a more cohesive brand presence. The badge appears on the far right of the top navigation bar or at the bottom of the hamburger menu. It links to Posit’s main website. @hadley is involved with this initiative.

The following websites already have the "Supported by Posit" badge: [ggplot2](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org), [Great Tables](https://posit-dev.github.io/great-tables/articles/intro.html), [gt](https://gt.rstudio.com), [Plotnine](https://plotnine.org), [Pointblank](https://posit-dev.github.io/pointblank/), [pointblank](https://rstudio.github.io/pointblank/), and [Quarto](https://quarto.org).

See https://posit-dev.github.io/supported-by-posit/ for more information.

## Changes

- Added a line to `_pkgdown.yml` to include the JavaScript file
- Standardized indentation in `_pkgdown.yml`

title: prefit xgboost model in `xrf_fit()`, allow early stopping
description:
This PR:

* Adds support for early stopping with `xrf::xrf()`
* Corrects routing of `mtry` from `colsample_bytree` to `colsample_bynode` (and is now thus consistent with parsnip, see tidymodels/parsnip#495)
* De-duplicates xgboost training code between parsnip and rules
* Extends testing for `xrf` engine and removes `mtry` tests that are now redundant with parsnip

It does so by making use of the `prefit_xgb` argument to `xrf::xrf()`—instead of having `xrf` handle the xgboost training, we use `parsnip::xgb_train` and pass the pre-fit xgboost model to `xrf`.

<details>
  <summary> Justification for pre-fitting </summary>
The pre-fitting makes some parts of wrapping easier for us, but was initially a need for early stopping:

 `xrf::xrf.formula()` wraps both `xgboost::xgb.train()` and `glmnet::glmnet()`. `xrf::xrf.formula()` takes in an `xgb_control` argument, where all arguments passed to `xgb_control` are passed to `xgboost::xbg.train()`'s `param` argument—this is currently the only way one can pass arguments to `xgboost::xgb.train()` through `xrf::xrf.formula()`.

This is an issue for early stopping, as `early_stopping_rounds` is a _main_ argument to `xgboost::xgb.train()` and cannot be passed through `param`. Thus, if we wanted to implement an interface for early stopping, we'd either:

* need to contribute to the xrf package to allow for passing arguments to `xrf::xrf.formula()` as main arguments to `xgboost::xbg.train()`
* "prefit" the xgboost model with our own machinery and pass it as `prefit_xgb` to `xrf::xrf.formula()`.

 </details>

Related to tidymodels/parsnip#749!

title: align `tunable` internals with parsnip
description:
While debugging tidymodels/parsnip\#351 yesterday, @juliasilge and I came across
some unexpected behavior related to `tunable` and passing along
engine-specific arguments.

``` r
install.packages("rules")
#> 
#> The downloaded binary packages are in
#>  /var/folders/qz/jqpclkqn0l9fkr5fr11xrzlh0000gn/T//Rtmp5l5YRt/downloaded_packages

library(rules)
#> Loading required package: modeldata
#> Loading required package: parsnip

packageVersion("rules")
#> [1] '0.2.0'
```

The functionality we’d hope for in passing along engine args, using `boost_tree`:

``` r
boost_tree() %>%
  set_mode("classification") %>%
  set_engine("C5.0", bands = tune()) %>%
  extract_parameter_set_dials()
#> Collection of 1 parameters for tuning
#> 
#>  identifier  type    object
#>       bands bands nparam[+]
```

What we see with `C5_rules`:

``` r
C5_rules() %>%
  set_engine("C5.0", fuzzyThreshold = tune()) %>%
  extract_parameter_set_dials()
#> Collection of 0 parameters for tuning
#> 
#> [1] identifier type       object    
#> <0 rows> (or 0-length row.names)
```

With more parsnip-like machinery, we can pass on engine-specific
arguments properly.

``` r
devtools::install_github("tidymodels/rules@tunable", quiet = TRUE)

library(rules)
#> Loading required package: parsnip

packageVersion("rules")
#> [1] '0.2.0.9000'

C5_rules() %>%
  set_engine("C5.0", fuzzyThreshold = tune()) %>%
  extract_parameter_set_dials()
#> Collection of 1 parameters for tuning
#> 
#>      identifier           type    object
#>  fuzzyThreshold fuzzyThreshold dparam[+]
```

This also made accommodating `min_n` tuning (\#27) straightforward.

``` r
C5_rules(min_n = tune()) %>%
  set_engine("C5.0") %>%
  extract_parameter_set_dials()
#> Collection of 1 parameters for tuning
#> 
#>  identifier  type    object
#>       min_n min_n nparam[+]
```

If this seems like a good move, I’ll walk through each of the remaining
model specs that need updates in tidymodels/parsnip\#691 and make sure
they pass on engine-specific arguments as they ought to as well. Once we
then update their `update()` their methods, they’ll be able to tune
engine-specific arguments!

Closes \#27, related to \#49.
